3. The petitioner in Writ Petition No. 863 of 1989 and the petitioners in Writ Petition 920 of 1989 claim to be the co-sharer and owner of the land measuring 0.0975 acres. It is stated in their respective petitions that the petitioner in Writ Petition No. 863 of 1989 along with one Abdul Hannan the petitioner Nos. 1-3 and the petitioner No. 4 Atar Banu of Writ Petition No. 920 of 1989 became owners of the land measuring 0.0975 acres equivalent to more or less 6 kathas of land of Plot. Nos. 119 and 120 and 253 appertaining to CS Khatian 84 of Mouza Tejturi Bazar JL No. 264 PS Tejgaon, District-Dhaka which was said to have been acquired under order dated 11.3.1989 passed by the Divisional Commissioner, Dhaka in LA Case No.9 of 1988-89 contained in Annexure-'F' of Writ Petition No. 863 of 1989 and Annexure-'E' of Writ Petition No. 920 of 1989. 

 7. At a later stage supplementary affidavit has been filed by the petitioners on 17.7.1994 with which photo copies of the khatian and some deeds have been annexed by which the petitioners sought to prove their title. The genuineness of the title deed has been disputed by the respondents stating that the documents have been filed at a belated stage. 

 10. From the perusal of the notice itself and the report submitted it appears that the notice under section 3 was served on the proceeding land and other places and, therefore, the petitioners cannot have grievance for not serving the notice personally on the petitioners claiming ownership of the proceeding land. The learned Advocate then argued that the notice under sections 3 and 6 do not contain the khatian number of the land sought to be acquired with proper specification and boundaries so as to enable the petitioners to raise objection. Mr. Saidur Rahman, the learned Assistant Attorney-General in reply submitted that the notice under sections 3 and 6 contained the plot number and the area of land measuring 0.0975 within mouza Testuribazar and the petitioners themselves having claimed that they had building over the land sought to be acquired we are of the view that the notice does not suffer from insufficiency and vagueness. From the statement made by the petitioners that they had a building which is alleged to have been demolished it appears that the petitioners were quite aware about the land sought to be acquired. Furthermore, this ground was not taken in the petition at the time of obtaining the Rule. For the aforesaid reasons we do not find substance in the above submission of the learned Advocate for the petitioners. Mr. TH Khan then argued that the power conferred to the authority to requisition property necessarily postulates a definite, specified and identifiable property but in the instant case the order of requisition purported to requisition a vague, indefinite and unidentifiable part of the petitioners land and hence it cannot be sustained.
